newsitem.title: TANZANIA: Christopher calls for closing Rwandan refugee camps.
newsitem.headline: Christopher calls for closing Rwandan refugee camps.

text.p: U.S. Secretary of State Warren Christopher called on Friday for the closure of Hutu refugee camps in Tanzania and Zaire that threaten the stability of Rwanda.
"We believe it is time to close the camps closest to the Rwandan border that pose the greatest security threat," he told a news conference after talks with African leaders on Burundi and Rwanda.
In a statement issued after the news conference, Christopher said the "refugees should be encouraged to return voluntarily to Rwanda, which we believe most can now do safely."
He added: "Where that is not possible they should be moved to camps further from the border."
There are some two million refugees, mostly members of the majority Hutu ethnic group, in camps in Tanzania and Zaire, on the border with Rwanda.

The refugees fled their homeland in 1994. Many were involved in the genocidal killings of one million Rwandans, mostly minority Tutsis, that led to renewed civil war. Many fear reprisals if they went back to Rwanda where a Tutsi-dominated army is now in control.
